note: Original leveled versions of every Reading Ladder passage: 'easier' (shorter sentences, same facts), the passage itself (on level), 'richer' (more detail and longer sentences, same facts), and a Spanish parallel version of the on-level text. The questions stay the same and stay English. A word asked about in a question appears in every English level. The Spanish version is machine-assisted and not reviewed by a human translator.

mina-bike.easier: Mina has a bike. It is red. It has a loud bell. Mina rides to school with her brother. They park by the gate. The road is busy. So they ride home slowly.
mina-bike.richer: Mina owns a bright red bike with a bell so loud that dogs bark when she rings it. Every morning she rides to school beside her older brother, and they lock their bikes by the front gate. After school they ride home slowly, because the road is busy with cars and buses.
mina-bike.es: Mina tiene una bicicleta roja. La bicicleta tiene un timbre fuerte. Todas las mañanas, Mina va a la escuela en bicicleta con su hermano. Dejan las bicicletas junto a la reja. Después de la escuela, vuelven a casa despacio porque la calle tiene mucho tráfico.

rain-day.easier: It rains on Monday. The children stay in the classroom. They read books. Sam reads about frogs. Lila draws the rain. At lunch, the sun comes out.
rain-day.richer: On Monday it rains all morning, so the children cannot go out to the playground. Instead they stay in the classroom and read. Sam chooses a book about frogs, and Lila draws a picture of the rain sliding down the window. At lunch, the clouds move away and the sun comes out.
rain-day.es: Llueve el lunes. Los niños no pueden jugar afuera. Se quedan en el salón y leen libros. Sam lee sobre ranas. Lila dibuja la lluvia. A la hora del almuerzo, sale el sol.

sleeping-cat.easier: Our cat is Pepper. Pepper sleeps a lot. In the morning, she sleeps on the sofa. In the afternoon, she sleeps by the window in a sunny spot. At night, she plays with a ball.
sleeping-cat.richer: Our cat, Pepper, spends most of the day asleep. In the morning she curls up on the sofa, and in the afternoon she moves to a sunny spot by the window where the light is warm. When night comes, she finally wakes up and chases a ball around the kitchen. Pepper is a busy cat at night!
sleeping-cat.es: Nuestra gata, Pepper, duerme mucho. Por la mañana duerme en el sofá. Por la tarde duerme en un lugar soleado junto a la ventana. De noche se despierta y juega con una pelota. ¡Pepper es una gata muy activa de noche!

lemonade-stand.easier: Ana and her cousin want a new soccer ball. They need money. So they make a lemonade stand. First, they make lemonade. Then they paint a sign. By noon, they sell twelve cups. "We are close!" Ana says.
lemonade-stand.richer: Ana and her cousin wanted to earn enough money for a new soccer ball, so they decided to open a lemonade stand on the corner. First they squeezed ten lemons and stirred in sugar and cold water. Then they painted a sign with big yellow letters so drivers could read it. By noon they had sold twelve cups. Ana counted the coins and smiled. "We need a few more customers," she said, "but we are close!"
lemonade-stand.es: Ana y su prima querían ganar dinero para un balón de fútbol nuevo, así que hicieron un puesto de limonada. Primero exprimieron diez limones y agregaron azúcar y agua fría. Luego pintaron un letrero con letras grandes y amarillas. Al mediodía habían vendido doce vasos. Ana sonrió y contó las monedas. "Necesitamos unos clientes más", dijo, "¡pero ya casi lo logramos!"

leaf-colors.easier: In the fall, many leaves change color. Leaves are green in summer. They have chlorophyll. Trees use it to make food. In the fall, trees make less of it. The green goes away. Red, orange and yellow were hidden. Now we can see them.
leaf-colors.richer: Every fall, many leaves turn from green to red, orange, and yellow. Leaves look green because they hold a substance called chlorophyll, which trees use to make food from sunlight. As the days get shorter and colder, trees make less chlorophyll. The green slowly fades, and the other colors, which were hidden underneath all summer, finally appear.
leaf-colors.es: En el otoño, muchas hojas cambian de verde a rojo, anaranjado y amarillo. Las hojas son verdes porque tienen una sustancia llamada clorofila. Los árboles la usan para hacer alimento con la luz del sol. Cuando los días se hacen más cortos, los árboles producen menos clorofila. El verde desaparece y los otros colores, que estuvieron escondidos todo el verano, se ven.

new-student.easier: Omar is a new student. He comes on Tuesday. He is very quiet. At recess, I ask him to play tag. He says no. Then he smiles and plays. After school, he says, "See you tomorrow!" I think he feels comfortable now.
new-student.richer: On Tuesday a new student named Omar joined our class. He spoke so quietly that the teacher had to lean in, and he held his backpack tightly all morning. At recess I invited him to play tag. At first he shook his head, but then he smiled and ran with us. After school he waved and said, "See you tomorrow!" I think he feels more comfortable now.
new-student.es: El martes, un estudiante nuevo llamado Omar llegó a nuestra clase. Hablaba en voz baja y sujetaba su mochila con fuerza. En el recreo, lo invité a jugar a la mancha. Primero dijo que no con la cabeza, pero luego sonrió y corrió con nosotros. Después de la escuela, saludó y dijo: "¡Hasta mañana!". Creo que ahora se siente más cómodo.

tide-pool.easier: The ocean tide goes out. Small pools of seawater stay in the rocks. The water is trapped there. Crabs, sea stars and snails live in these tide pools. At low tide, the water gets hot and salty. At high tide, big waves hit the rocks. Hard shells and strong arms help the animals stay safe.
tide-pool.richer: When the ocean tide goes out, small pools of seawater stay trapped among the rocks along the shore. These tide pools are home to crabs, sea stars, and snails, and every animal there must survive difficult changes each day. At low tide the sun heats the shallow water until it becomes salty, and at high tide strong waves crash over the rocks. Many of these animals have hard shells or strong arms that hold on tightly, which helps them stay safe in both conditions.
tide-pool.es: Cuando la marea del océano baja, pequeñas pozas de agua de mar quedan atrapadas entre las rocas. Estas pozas de marea son el hogar de cangrejos, estrellas de mar y caracoles. Los animales que viven allí deben sobrevivir cambios difíciles. Con la marea baja, el sol calienta el agua y se vuelve salada. Con la marea alta, olas fuertes chocan contra las rocas. Muchos animales tienen conchas duras o brazos fuertes que se sujetan bien, y eso los ayuda a estar seguros en las dos situaciones.

broken-window.easier: Marcus plays baseball in the backyard. He hits the ball too hard. Crash! The ball breaks his neighbor's window. Marcus could hide. But that does not feel right. He goes to Mrs. Lopez's door. "I'm sorry," he says. "I will pay to fix it." Mrs. Lopez thanks him for his honesty.
broken-window.richer: While practicing baseball in the backyard, Marcus swung harder than ever and heard a loud crash. The ball had gone straight through his neighbor's window. His heart pounded. He could run inside and pretend nothing had happened, but that did not feel right to him. Slowly, he walked next door to Mrs. Lopez's house and knocked. "I'm sorry," he said. "I will use my savings to fix it." Mrs. Lopez thanked him for his honesty and told him that accidents happen to everyone.
broken-window.es: Mientras practicaba béisbol en el patio, Marcus golpeó la pelota demasiado fuerte y oyó un ruido fuerte. La pelota había roto la ventana de su vecina. El corazón le latía con fuerza. Podía entrar a la casa y fingir que no había pasado nada, pero eso no le parecía correcto. Despacio, caminó hasta la puerta de la señora López y tocó. "Lo siento", dijo. "Voy a usar mis ahorros para arreglarla." La señora López le agradeció su honestidad y le dijo que los accidentes pasan.

bookmobile.easier: Some people live far from a library. So some towns send a bookmobile. A bookmobile is a bus full of books. It comes on a schedule. Families know when it will come. Children and adults borrow books. For some families, it is the only way to get books.
bookmobile.richer: In some rural areas, families live many miles from the nearest library. To help them, some communities send out a bookmobile, which is a bus filled with shelves of books. The bookmobile visits villages on a regular schedule, so families know exactly when to come. Children borrow picture books, while adults borrow novels and cookbooks, and some buses even offer free internet. For many families, the bookmobile is the only way to reach books at all.
bookmobile.es: En algunas zonas rurales, las personas viven lejos de una biblioteca. Para ayudarlas, algunas comunidades envían un bibliobús, que es un autobús lleno de libros. El bibliobús visita los pueblos según un horario, así que las familias saben cuándo ir. Los niños piden prestados libros ilustrados y los adultos piden novelas y libros de cocina. Algunos autobuses también ofrecen internet gratis. Para muchas familias, el bibliobús es la única manera de conseguir libros.

waggle-dance.easier: Honeybees cannot talk. But they can show where food is. A bee finds flowers. She goes back to the hive. She performs a waggle dance. She moves in a figure eight and shakes. The angle of the dance shows the direction. The length of the shaking shows how far the flowers are. Other bees watch. Then they fly to the flowers.
waggle-dance.richer: Honeybees cannot talk, yet they can tell one another exactly where to find food. When a worker bee discovers a field of flowers, she flies back to the hive and performs a "waggle dance" on the honeycomb. She moves in a figure-eight pattern and shakes her body in the middle of each loop. The angle of the dance shows the direction of the flowers compared with the sun, while the length of the shaking shows how far away they are. Other workers watch closely and then fly out to collect nectar. Scientists have studied this dance for decades because it is one of the few known examples of animals sharing detailed information.
waggle-dance.es: Las abejas no pueden hablar, pero pueden decirse exactamente dónde encontrar comida. Cuando una abeja obrera descubre un campo de flores, regresa a la colmena y realiza una "danza del meneo". Se mueve en forma de ocho y sacude el cuerpo en el centro. El ángulo de la danza muestra la dirección de las flores con respecto al sol, y la duración del meneo muestra qué tan lejos están. Las otras obreras observan con atención y luego salen a recoger néctar. Los científicos han estudiado esta danza durante décadas porque es uno de los pocos ejemplos de animales que comparten información detallada.

clock-tower.easier: The old clock tower in Alder Creek is quiet for years. People argue. Fix it or tear it down? Priya is twelve. She loves gears. She climbs the stairs. She finds one bent gear. An old watchmaker helps her fix it. At noon, the bells ring! Many people thought it was hopeless. Patience and teamwork solved the problem.
clock-tower.richer: In the town of Alder Creek, the old clock tower had stood silent for years, and residents argued at every meeting about whether to repair it or tear it down. Twelve-year-old Priya, who loved gears and springs, volunteered to inspect it herself. After climbing the dusty spiral stairs, she discovered that a single bent gear had stopped the whole mechanism. With help from the town's retired watchmaker, she carefully straightened it. At noon the bells rang for the first time in years, and the crowd below cheered. Priya realized that patience and teamwork had solved a problem that others thought was hopeless.
clock-tower.es: En el pueblo de Alder Creek, la vieja torre del reloj llevaba años en silencio. Los vecinos discutían si debían repararla o derribarla. Priya, de doce años, a quien le encantaban los engranajes y los resortes, se ofreció a revisarla. Después de subir las escaleras llenas de polvo, descubrió que un solo engranaje doblado había detenido el mecanismo. Con la ayuda del relojero jubilado del pueblo, lo enderezó. Al mediodía, las campanas sonaron por primera vez en años y la gente abajo aplaudió. Priya entendió que la paciencia y el trabajo en equipo habían resuelto un problema que otros creían imposible.

aluminum-cans.easier: Aluminum cans can be recycled many times. Recycling a can uses about ninety-five percent less energy than making a new can. A truck takes the cans. A factory melts them. The metal becomes new cans. The metal is reused, so fewer mines are needed. Less trash goes to landfills.
aluminum-cans.richer: Aluminum cans can be recycled again and again without losing any quality. In fact, recycling a can uses about ninety-five percent less energy than making a new one from raw material dug out of the ground. The process starts when a truck collects the cans; then a factory shreds and melts them, and the melted metal is rolled into sheets that are made into new cans. This entire cycle can take as little as sixty days. Because the metal is reused, fewer mines are needed, and much less trash goes to landfills.
aluminum-cans.es: Las latas de aluminio se pueden reciclar una y otra vez sin perder calidad. Reciclar una lata usa alrededor de un noventa y cinco por ciento menos de energía que fabricar una nueva con materia prima. El proceso empieza cuando un camión recoge las latas y una fábrica las tritura y las derrite. El metal derretido se convierte en láminas, que luego se usan para hacer latas nuevas. Todo el ciclo puede durar solo sesenta días. Como el metal se reutiliza, se necesitan menos minas y llega menos basura a los vertederos.

green-roofs.easier: In big cities, many roofs are dark. They get very hot in summer. This makes the neighborhood hotter. A green roof is a roof with soil and plants. The vegetation gives shade. It also cools the air. It soaks up rain, so streets flood less. A green roof costs more at first. But it can save money later.
green-roofs.richer: In crowded cities, most rooftops are bare surfaces of tar and gravel that absorb heat all day. On hot summer afternoons these dark roofs can become much warmer than the surrounding air, raising the temperature of the whole neighborhood. To address this problem, some architects design green roofs, which are rooftops covered with soil and living plants. The vegetation shades the building and releases water vapor, which cools the air around it. A green roof also soaks up rainwater, reducing the amount that rushes into storm drains and floods the streets below. Although installing one costs more than building a traditional roof, supporters argue that lower energy bills and a longer roof life eventually make up the difference.
green-roofs.es: En las ciudades con mucha gente, los techos suelen ser superficies de brea y grava que absorben el calor. En los días calurosos de verano, estos techos oscuros pueden calentarse mucho más que el aire, y suben la temperatura de todo el barrio. Para resolver este problema, algunos arquitectos diseñan techos verdes, que son techos cubiertos de tierra y plantas. La vegetación da sombra al edificio y suelta vapor de agua, que enfría el aire. Un techo verde también absorbe el agua de lluvia y reduce la cantidad que corre hacia las alcantarillas y que inunda las calles. Aunque instalarlo cuesta más que un techo tradicional, quienes lo apoyan dicen que las cuentas de energía más bajas y la vida más larga del techo compensan la diferencia con el tiempo.

lighthouse-keeper.easier: Mr. Okafor worked at the Gull Point lighthouse for forty years. Every evening, he lit the lamp. Ships depended on the light. It kept them away from the rocks. Then automatic lights replaced the keepers. Mr. Okafor did not complain. On his last night, he wrote, "The light still turns." Today, children read his words at the museum.
lighthouse-keeper.richer: For more than forty years, Mr. Okafor climbed the spiral staircase of the Gull Point lighthouse every evening to light the great lamp at the top. Ships depended on that turning beam to steer clear of the jagged rocks below. When automatic lights replaced human keepers, the harbor office announced that his services were no longer required. Mr. Okafor did not complain. On his final night, he polished the glass lens one last time and wrote a single line in the logbook: "The light still turns." Years later, schoolchildren visiting the museum read the entry and understood that his work, though now done by machines, had once protected many lives.
lighthouse-keeper.es: Durante más de cuarenta años, el señor Okafor subió la escalera de caracol del faro de Gull Point cada tarde para encender la gran lámpara. Los barcos dependían de esa luz para evitar las rocas afiladas de abajo. Cuando las luces automáticas reemplazaron a los guardianes, la oficina del puerto anunció que ya no necesitaban su trabajo. El señor Okafor no se quejó. En su última noche, pulió la lente una última vez y escribió en el libro de registro: "La luz todavía gira". Años después, los estudiantes que visitaban el museo leyeron esa nota y entendieron que su trabajo, aunque ahora lo hacen máquinas, antes protegió muchas vidas.

new-language.easier: Many adults think children learn languages effortlessly. Research says it is not that simple. Young children learn sounds fast. Older learners know grammar rules. They know how to study. In one study, teenagers learned some grammar faster than children. Regular practice helps learners of every age the most.
new-language.richer: Many adults believe that children learn new languages effortlessly, but research suggests that the real picture is more complicated. Young children do absorb sounds quickly, and they often develop pronunciation that sounds native. However, older learners usually have advantages of their own: they understand grammar rules, can use strategies for memorizing vocabulary, and already know how to study. In one study, teenagers actually learned certain grammar patterns faster than younger children did. The best results appear to come from regular practice and many chances to use the language in real conversations, no matter how old the learner is.
new-language.es: Muchos adultos creen que los niños aprenden idiomas sin esfuerzo, pero las investigaciones indican que la situación es más complicada. Los niños pequeños sí captan los sonidos rápidamente y a menudo logran una pronunciación como la de un hablante nativo. Sin embargo, los estudiantes mayores suelen tener sus propias ventajas: entienden las reglas gramaticales, pueden usar estrategias para memorizar vocabulario y saben estudiar. En un estudio, los adolescentes aprendieron ciertos patrones gramaticales más rápido que los niños más pequeños. Los mejores resultados parecen venir de la práctica regular y de muchas oportunidades para usar el idioma, sin importar la edad.

immune-training.easier: Your immune system fights germs. When it encounters a new germ, it needs a few days to learn how to fight it. A person can get sick during that time. A vaccine helps. It has a harmless piece of the germ. The body learns to know the germ. It makes memory cells. If the real germ comes, memory cells act fast. So vaccines are training, not treatment.
immune-training.richer: Your immune system protects the body from invaders such as bacteria and viruses. The first time it encounters a new germ, it needs several days to identify the threat and produce the right defenses, and during that delay a person can become seriously ill. A vaccine offers a safer way to gain that experience in advance. It contains a harmless piece or a weakened form of the germ, which is enough for the immune system to recognize it but not enough to cause the disease. The body responds by building antibodies and creating memory cells that can remain for many years. If the real germ ever appears, these memory cells launch a rapid response, often stopping the infection before any symptoms begin. This is why scientists describe vaccines as training rather than treatment.
immune-training.es: Tu sistema inmunitario protege el cuerpo de invasores como las bacterias y los virus. La primera vez que se encuentra con un germen nuevo, necesita varios días para reconocer la amenaza y producir las defensas correctas, y durante ese tiempo una persona puede enfermarse gravemente. Una vacuna ofrece una manera más segura de ganar esa experiencia. Contiene una parte inofensiva o una forma debilitada del germen, suficiente para que el sistema inmunitario lo reconozca pero no para causar la enfermedad. El cuerpo responde formando anticuerpos y creando células de memoria que duran años. Si el germen real aparece, esas células de memoria responden rápidamente y muchas veces detienen la infección antes de que empiecen los síntomas. Por eso se dice que las vacunas son un entrenamiento y no un tratamiento.

market-change.easier: Lucía saved money for a scarf for her grandmother. At the market, the vendor gave her too much change. Lucía could keep it. No one saw. But the vendor looked tired. She counted her coins nervously. Lucía hesitated. Then she gave the money back. The vendor thanked her. Lucía felt lighter on the way home.
market-change.richer: Lucía had saved for months to buy her grandmother a wool scarf at the weekend market. When she paid, however, she noticed that the vendor had mistakenly given her extra change, enough to buy a second scarf. Her first instinct was to walk away quietly; after all, no one had noticed the mistake. Yet the vendor, an older woman with tired eyes, was counting her coins nervously as customers drifted past her table. Lucía hesitated, then turned around and returned the money. The vendor's face softened. "Not everyone would have come back," she said. Lucía only shrugged, but as she carried the scarf home she felt lighter than she had all week.
market-change.es: Lucía había ahorrado durante meses para comprarle una bufanda a su abuela en el mercado del fin de semana. Pero al llegar, se dio cuenta de que una vendedora le había dado cambio de más por error, suficiente para comprar una segunda bufanda. Lo primero que pensó fue irse en silencio; al fin y al cabo, nadie lo había notado. Pero la vendedora, una mujer mayor de mirada cansada, contaba sus monedas con nerviosismo mientras los clientes pasaban de largo. Lucía dudó y luego devolvió el dinero. La cara de la vendedora se suavizó. "No todos habrían vuelto", dijo. Lucía se encogió de hombros, pero mientras llevaba la bufanda a casa se sintió más ligera que en toda la semana.

sound-waves.easier: Sound starts when something vibrates. The air particles bump into each other. The vibrations travel to your ear. Your brain can interpret them. Sound needs particles, so it cannot travel through empty space. Sound moves faster in water than in air. It moves even faster in steel. So you can hear a train through a railroad track before you hear it in the air.
sound-waves.richer: Sound is created when an object vibrates, causing the surrounding air particles to bump into one another in a chain reaction. This wave of vibrations travels outward until it reaches your ear, where tiny structures translate it into signals that your brain can interpret. Because sound depends on particles to carry it, it cannot travel through the empty space between planets. Interestingly, it moves faster through water than through air, and faster still through steel, because the particles in denser materials are packed closer together and pass vibrations along more quickly. This explains why a person who presses an ear against a railroad track can detect an approaching train long before its sound arrives through the air.
sound-waves.es: El sonido se produce cuando un objeto vibra y hace que las partículas del aire choquen unas con otras en una reacción en cadena. Esta onda de vibraciones viaja hasta llegar a tu oído, donde unas estructuras muy pequeñas la convierten en señales que tu cerebro puede interpretar. Como el sonido necesita partículas para viajar, no puede atravesar el espacio vacío. Curiosamente, se mueve más rápido en el agua que en el aire, y todavía más rápido en el acero, porque las partículas de los materiales más densos están más juntas y pasan las vibraciones con más rapidez. Por eso una persona que pone el oído sobre una vía de tren puede notar que se acerca un tren mucho antes de oírlo por el aire.
